## Critic round 1 — REVISE, 1 blocker, FIXED

The v2 gotchas draft asserted the inner exception is retained "only [in]
`__context__`, and no traceback line surfaces it". **False.** PEP 3134 implicit
chaining makes the DEFAULT traceback print the inner exception under `During
handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:`, and
`logger.exception` logs the same chain. Verified by live reproduction (inner
`ValueError`, `TimeoutError` raised in `finally`): traceback shows both;
`f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"` shows only the `TimeoutError`.

The real masking channel is any consumer that formats only the FINAL exception.
#1947's is `scripts/issue1947_worker.py:1005-1013` — `logger.exception` at :1006
held the full chain, while `reason: f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"` at :1010, the
field the orchestrator triages from, held only the teardown error.

This mattered because the deliverable IS the claim: the v2 wording would have
taught the next debugger that the traceback cannot hold the real error,
suppressing the single fastest recognition step — reading the `During handling`
block, which would have ended #1947 at round 1.

v3-v5 therefore document BOTH sides: the raise side (detect-in-flight, then
suppress-and-log or chain) AND the reporting side (a per-unit failure record
carries the chain, not `str(e)`), so the mask cannot re-form downstream of a
correctly-guarded teardown. Acceptance criteria 2 + 2b pin the corrected
mechanism against regression in any rewording round.
